label: 0021 · Starter, 50 km BEL cut, Nankai and Japan Trench remeshed with elements that grow away from the stations (up to 40 km at the trench; 5 km at Hyuga-nada), -20 floor after the 2024 Hyuga-nada earthquake, CMT catalog through May 2025, UNR positions (exploratory MCMC)
description: 0020 with both trench meshes remeshed so that the element size grows with the distance from the nearest station: the base size within 60 km (16 km for Nankai, 12 km for the Japan Trench), growing in proportion up to 40 km. The Japan Trench mesh has 1664 triangles instead of 3048, with ~30 km elements at the trench. Nankai keeps 0020's 5 km Hyuga-nada zone, gets ~30 km elements at the trench off Kyushu and Shikoku and 16 km again at the Suruga Trough (2322 triangles). The Japan Trench keeps a fixed 64 km length scale (area-weighted modes); Nankai's follows the element size as in 0020 (75 modes). The results match 0020: the fit in every window is within 0.3%, coupling moves by a median of 0.07 (Nankai) and 0.09 (Japan Trench) posterior standard deviations, and Tohoku afterslip is unchanged. In Aug-Dec 2024 the Hyuga-nada afterslip covers 3,400 km2 at 18-39 km depth (0020: 3,700 km2 at 17-42 km). In scratch tests a length scale that follows the element size on the coarse Japan Trench mesh moved unresolved postseismic slip to the trench, so it is not used there. Block motion is that of 0012-0020 (reference solve reused).
